decision.detail: I stand up from the lobby chair. I peel my coat off the back. I lift my bag by the strap and set it on my shoulder. I walk to the front door, push it open. The February air hits my face. I don't look back at the lobby, the piano, the coffee table. I walk toward the station. The coach is at the platform. I have the ticket. I board. I sit. I put my bag on the floor between my feet. The bus pulls out. The town slides by the window. I watch it go. I don't play the bars. I don't sit in the folding chair. I ride. I ride all the way. I get off at the terminal in Pittsburgh. I walk to the payphone. I put the coins in. I dial. I say: Hi, is the van driver still confirming for 8 AM tomorrow? I'm at the terminal now. I hang up. I sit on the bench. I wait. The evening comes. The evening is different or it isn't. I don't need it to be different. I need to be here. In the body of a man on a bench in a city that is not the hotel. That is the weight. That is the thing. Not the shape. The weight.
decision.intention: Be in Pittsburgh. Be at the terminal. Make the call. Confirm the van. Be there when the couch needs moving. Do the thing. Not test the shape. Do the thing.
decision.words: I turn to Rita and Larry. I say: I'm heading to the station. Coach to Pittsburgh. I'll be back by the party, or I won't be. Either way. I pick up my bag. I walk out the door. I don't wait for an answer. I don't need one.
